thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SRV lookup error spike in us-east1a impacting service discovery for redwood-dedicated pools. 30% of requests are falling back. Paging oncall now.

alex: acked. I'm on it. can someone paste quick customer impact numbers?

marta: seeing a big uptick in `x-service-unavailable` from model-proxy in us-east1a. Canary traffic for a handful of customers is failing to connect to backend pods.

leo: model endpoints 0.2% of overall traffic but for 3 customers it's hitting 50% of their requests -> retries and elevated latency.

priya: I'm rolling up logs. preliminary looks like SRV queries returning different sets of targets from different resolvers (some old targets still present). looks like a stale SRV cache.

raj: support-bot: I've opened a ticket and pinged the two affected customer owners with interim note.

alex: can you confirm whether this is coredns or consul side? we had a similar pattern when we saw TTL mismatches last quarter.

marta: from pod-level debug: `dig +short _redwood._tcp.svc.consul SRV @10.0.0.10` on a node in us-east1a returns 3 entries including two deprecated targets. same query against us-east1b returns the updated set.

priya: running `curl http://127.0.0.1:9153/metrics | grep coredns_cache` on coredns shows high miss/evict churn. suspicious.

infra-bot: automated alert: consul leader observed transient write latency spike at 2028-12-13T18:25:02Z (p90 raft apply 1.8s).

alex: ok likely race during consul leader failover earlier that left some SRV records inconsistent across agents. mitigation options: force coredns cache flush in us-east1a, roll consul agents in small window, or route traffic away from us-east1a via smart routing.

priya: I'm going to flush coredns caches on all nodes in us-east1a first. command: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=coredns -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl -n kube-system exec {} -- coredns-ctl cache flush
```
(I have a safer version that curls the metrics endpoint to evict entries if needed).

marta: doing a targeted coredns restart on one node to validate: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod coredns-6f8b9d -n kube-system` (will be reclaimed). I'll rotate gradually.

leo: also recommend a temporary policy to prefer us-east1b/1c for routing SRV lookups for affected customers while we validate. we can add a routing override in the proxy layer for those customer IDs.

alex: agreed. raj, can you coordinate with support to message customers with short ETA?

raj: yes, sending a brief: "We're seeing service discovery inconsistencies in us-east1a causing intermittent failovers. We are mitigating by flushing caches and routing traffic; next update in 30m." sending now.

infra-bot: action log: started coredns flush on 3 nodes in us-east1a by priya at 18:29:10Z.

priya: flush done on first node, SRV response now matches us-east1b. running for remaining nodes.

marta: after two nodes flushed, error rate dropped from 30%->7% for affected customer traffic. continuing.

alex: good. do we know root cause? why stale entries remained post-consul leader failover?

priya: preliminary: some consul agents in us-east1a were still serving cached catalog entries due to a bug around TTL renewal when leader changed. i've opened a consul issue and will grab raft logs: `consul debug raft`

deploy-bot: note: a small consul agent restart has been queued (rolling) to pick up the hotfix flag; will proceed with manual approval.

alex: hold on the roll until we confirm cache flush stabilizes. rolling consul agents can cause more transient flips.

leo: meanwhile i've pushed a routing override for the two affected customers to prefer other AZs. this should reduce customer impact to near-zero while we investigate. ruleset: `route_preference: us-east1b,us-east1c,us-east1a` applied to customer ids.

support-bot: support message posted: "We're mitigating SRV discovery instability in us-east1a; routing temporarily adjusted. You may see reduced latency and fewer errors. We'll follow up with post-incident details."

priya: flush completed on all us-east1a coredns nodes at 18:37:52Z. SRV consistency verified across AZs.

marta: monitoring: error rate stable at baseline ~0.5%. rolling back routing override in 10m if stable.

alex: thanks all. preparing handoff to night oncall—priyaa? (typo) Priya, can you take the ongoing watch and runbook items for follow-up?

priya: i'm happy to take it. items: 1) collect consul raft logs for 18:20-18:30 window 2) capture coredns cache metrics and eviction traces 3) follow up on consul TTL renewal bug and link to internal issue 4) coordinate a low-risk consul agent rolling restart in a maintenance window next week.

alex: added to the incident doc. customer impact summary for comms: "Intermittent SRV resolution inconsistencies in us-east1a caused transient request failures affecting a small subset of dedicated customers. Mitigation (coredns cache flush + temporary routing override) restored consistency and reduced errors to baseline within ~10 minutes. Remediations: consul TTL/leadership bug investigation, planned agent maintenance, and an improvement to our SRV cache invalidation logic."

raj: i'll follow up with impacted customers with that summary and estimated timeline for postmortem. sending now.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status -> mitigated. Incident lead: alex. Handoff -> priya. Postmortem ETA 48 hours.

priya: taking watch. will post findings and attach logs to the incident doc. :wave:

alex: great job team. closing on-call marker here. we'll add remediation tickets and track SLA impact in finance dashboard.

support-bot: ticket updated with incident id INC-2028-1459 and customer notes.

marta: I'm adding a follow-up to track automated cache eviction mechanism testing.

leo: also adding an alert to detect SRV divergence across AZs (diff check every 5m).

priya: last check at 18:43:30Z: SRV parity confirmed across AZs, error rates normal. handoff complete.

alex: thanks all.
